candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the XML document (or any stream/Reader/InputSource) submitted to the application for parsing. Within that document the attacker fully controls DOCTYPE declarations, external entity declarations (`<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///...">` or `SYSTEM "http://attacker/...">`) and their use in content, so both the entity system identifier and the point of expansion are attacker-chosen.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The API does offer hardening hooks, so this is a defaults problem rather than an unconditional flaw: callers can call setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true) or setFeature(SAX_FEATURE_EXTERNAL_ENT, false) (SAXBuilder.java:797-801), set an EntityResolver (lines 564-567), or provide a custom XMLReaderJDOMFactory. `setExpandEntities(false)` also causes the external-general-entities feature to be set false (lines 719-722, 991-996). The feature-setting block swallows SAXException (lines 995-996), so on parsers lacking the feature the behavior falls back to that parser's default rather than being disabled by JDOM. No runtime verification was performed and no code executed; the Java/JAXP default of external entity resolution being enabled is an environment assumption. However, JDOM's own default explicitly enables the feature, and repository-wide searches confirm the absence of disallow-doctype-decl, external-parameter-entities, load-external-dtd, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, or ACCESS_EXTERNAL_* anywhere, and no default EntityResolver is installed.
candidates.impact: XML External Entity injection against any application that uses the default JDOM SAXBuilder on untrusted XML: (a) disclosure of local files/streams (e.g. configuration, credentials, /etc/passwd) into the parsed document, which is then visible wherever the application consumes or re-serializes the JDOM tree; (b) server-side request forgery / port probing via external entity or external DTD SYSTEM identifiers; (c) denial of service through large or blocking external resources (in addition to internal entity expansion, which modern parsers partially limit). These are the same class of attacks tracked publicly as the JDOM SAXBuilder XXE issue; this snapshot contains no default mitigation.
candidates.prerequisites: The host application uses JDOM's default parsing configuration (e.g. `new SAXBuilder()` or the equivalent default XMLReaderJDOMFactory `XMLReaders.NONVALIDATING`) and feeds it untrusted XML without explicitly calling `setFeature(...)`, `setEntityResolver(...)`, or supplying a pre-hardened custom `XMLReaderJDOMFactory`. The underlying SAX parser must support the external-general-entities feature (standard JDK/JAXP Xerces does, defaulting to enabled); JDOM's own code sets it to true and no code path disables DOCTYPE processing.
candidates.root_cause: SAXBuilder is pre-configured for entity expansion (`private boolean expand = true`, SAXBuilder.java:195-196) and `configureParser()` actively sets the parser feature `http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities` to that value (SAXBuilder.java:991-996). Because the default is true, the feature is enabled on the parser. The same method installs a user EntityResolver only when one was supplied (SAXBuilder.java:933-935), so by default the parser's own resolver is used, and no `disallow-doctype-decl`, `external-parameter-entities=false`, `load-external-dtd=false`, or `XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING` configuration exists anywhere in the codebase (verified by repository-wide search: zero matches). Parsed content is passed straight to the XMLReader (`SAXBuilderEngine.build`, SAXBuilderEngine.java:213-219 → `saxParser.parse(in)`), and SAXHandler expands resolved entity characters into normal Text content when `expand` is true (SAXBuilder.buildEngine, SAXBuilder.java:848-850).
candidates.title: Default SAXBuilder configuration enables external entity expansion (XXE) when parsing untrusted XML
candidates.trace: 1) `new SAXBuilder()` selects `XMLReaders.NONVALIDATING` and leaves `expand = true` (SAXBuilder.java:336-347, 195-196). 2) `build(InputStream/Reader/InputSource/File/URL)` calls `getEngine()`/`buildEngine()` (SAXBuilder.java:1087-1097, 845-860). 3) `buildEngine()` calls `configureParser(parser, contentHandler)` (SAXBuilder.java:854-856); `configureParser` sets a custom EntityResolver only if the user supplied one (lines 933-935) and then, because `expand == true`, sets `http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities` to true (lines 991-996). 4) `SAXBuilderEngine.build()` invokes `saxParser.parse(in)` on the attacker-supplied document (SAXBuilderEngine.java:213-219). 5) The parser resolves declared external entities and routes their content through SAXHandler.characters; with expansion enabled the data becomes Text nodes in the returned JDOM Document (SAXHandler.java:296-298; SAXBuilder.java:848-850), and external SYSTEM URLs are also fetched by the parser for SSRF/DoS.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: I did not execute a parser or payload, and I did not diff against upstream releases to identify the exact fix commit. Whether a specific deployment is exploitable depends on the JAXP/SAX parser in use and on the application not having applied the available hardening calls; behavior of non-supporting SAX parsers could differ (the exception at SAXBuilder.java:995 is swallowed).
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reported 261 model-visible text files (no excluded/symlinked/binary files; same filters for B0/P1). I focused on the core XML parsing stack: SAXBuilder (constructors, build methods, configureParser, feature/property handling), SAXBuilderEngine, SAXHandler entity handling, XMLReaders and the XMLReader*Factory classes, JDOMConstants, plus DOMBuilder, StAXStreamBuilder/StAXEventBuilder, DOMOutputter/XMLOutputter escape paths (Format, AbstractXMLOutputProcessor), XSLTransformer/JDOMSource/JDOMResult, internal helpers (SystemProperty, ReflectionConstructor), and the contrib packages at survey level. Repository-wide searches were used for hardening/security keywords (disallow-doctype-decl, external-parameter-entities, load-external-dtd, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, ACCESS_EXTERNAL_*, resolveEntity, setFeature, setAccessible, Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder, readObject). Not every one of the 261 files was read line-by-line.
limitations: No code execution, tests, scanners, or payloads were run; findings remain source-evidence leads and are not runtime-confirmed.
No upstream diff/history was available, so I could not confirm which release/commit this snapshot corresponds to or what the official fix changed.

Exact exploitability depends on the deployed JAXP/SAX parser defaults and on whether the consuming application hardens SAXBuilder or treats input as trusted; those runtime/deployment facts are outside the snapshot.
Deep line-by-line review was concentrated on input/parsing and output escaping; XPath/Jaxen, Verifier, StringBin, located/*, and some output/support classes were only surveyed.

rejected_leads.lead: XSLTransformer builds TransformerFactory with no secure-processing or external-access restrictions (core/src/java/org/jdom2/transform/XSLTransformer.java:124-135).
rejected_leads.reason: The stylesheet is normally trusted application input, JDOM treats it as such, and exploitation requires an attacker-controlled XSLT, so attacker control/impact is weaker and less clear than the default SAXBuilder XXE.

rejected_leads.lead: contrib JDOMBean.getDocument(String filename) constructs `new File(filename)` from its argument with the intended file-root confinement commented out and says so in its own javadoc (contrib/src/java/org/jdom2/contrib/beans/JDOMBean.java:204-239).
rejected_leads.reason: Contrib demo/helper class with the caveat documented in-source; it is not part of the core parsing path and requires the application to pass user input as a filename.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLReaders XSD singleton creates SchemaFactory without ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA/DTD restrictions (core/src/java/org/jdom2/input/sax/XMLReaders.java:154-206).
rejected_leads.reason: Only relevant when validating against caller-supplied schemas; no evidence of attacker-controlled schema or entity expansion.
They explicitly document that XMLStreamReader configuration (including entity handling) is the caller's responsibility; JDOM does not control the input factory.

Reviewed Format.escapeAttribute/escapeText (core/src/java/org/jdom2/output/Format.java:346-430); required characters including quotes, ampersands, CR/LF/TAB and surrogates are escaped, and raw output is only used when escaping is explicitly disabled.

summary: The snapshot is the JDOM 2.x core (plus contrib/samples). The strongest security-relevant behavior found is the default XML input configuration of `org.jdom2.input.SAXBuilder`: it expands entities by default and explicitly turns on the SAX `external-general-entities` feature, while installing no default `EntityResolver` and applying no DOCTYPE-disabling / secure-processing features. Any application that parses untrusted XML with the documented default `new SAXBuilder().build(...)` is therefore left explicitly exposed to classic XXE (local file disclosure into the JDOM tree, SSRF via external entity SYSTEM ids, and external-resource denial of service). No other candidate in the snapshot had comparable attacker control plus concrete impact.
